analysis:
This feature adds a fourth TEST_EDIT_REASON escape valve ('mock_structure') enabling the autofix implementer to declare a structural test-rewrite handoff instead of emitting UNRESOLVED and triggering wasteful tier escalation. The change spans 5 interdependent stories across 9+ source files.

**Dependency chain:** US-001 (parser) → US-002 (validator + side-channel) → US-004 (strategy wiring) → US-005 (guards + config). US-003 (prompts) is independent and can run in parallel.

**Key architectural decision — FindingSource extension:** The synthetic findings synthesized in US-002 use `source: "implementer-handoff"`. The current `FindingSource` union in `src/findings/types.ts` does NOT include this value. US-002 implementer MUST add `"implementer-handoff"` to `FindingSource` or TypeScript strict mode will reject the code. This is an implicit but mandatory change.

**`applyTestEditDeclarations` stays pure/sync:** All I/O is in `validateMockStructureFiles` (async). The existing `applyTestEditDeclarations` function must remain synchronous. US-002 extends it (likely with an optional 4th parameter for the invalid partition) to produce advisory findings for invalid declarations while keeping source-tagged findings unchanged.

**Side-channel follows existing `testEditDeclarations` pattern:** `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs` is populated by `validate()` (stash), consumed one-shot by `buildInput` in the test-writer strategy (clear on read). US-004 must clear the array after consumption.

**`beforeRef` for guards (US-005):** Guards diff against the git HEAD captured *just before* the test-writer op starts in `mock-restructure` mode. The implementation must call `git rev-parse HEAD` at that point — the existing `ctx.storyGitRef` is per-story-iteration (set before execution), not per-op.

**Guard revert semantics:** Guards run post-commit (after the test-writer op completes). `revertDiff(workdir, files)` runs `git checkout HEAD -- <files>` to undo the test-writer's changes. The cycle then records the failed iteration and exits via the existing `agent-gave-up` rail — NOT a new exit path.

**Existing test files to extend:** `test/unit/operations/test-edit-declaration.test.ts`, `test/unit/pipeline/stages/autofix-cycle.test.ts`, `test/unit/prompts/builders/rectifier-builder.test.ts`, `test/integration/autofix-implementer-feedback.test.ts`. Check these paths exist before implementing; the integration test file may need to be created if absent.

**Config schema location:** The autofix Zod schema lives in `src/config/schemas-execution.ts`. The hand-maintained default literal is in `src/config/schemas.ts` at the `quality.autofix` key (lines ~147-153 at commit 01cdda7e). The runtime-types interface is in `src/config/runtime-types.ts` at `QualityConfig.autofix` (lines ~209-220).

**`validate()` orchestration order (US-002):** (1) `recheckReview`, (2) `resolveTestFilePatterns` + `validateMockStructureFiles`, (3) populate `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs` from valid partition, (4) call `applyTestEditDeclarations` with both valid and invalid mock_structure declarations, (5) clear `ctx.testEditDeclarations`.

**`buildAutofixStrategies` is called with the outer `ctx` closed over:** The testWriter `buildInput` already closes over `ctx` via the outer function scope. US-004 extends this closure to read and clear `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs`.

**`_gitDeps.spawn` pattern (US-005):** `src/utils/git.ts` exports `_gitDeps` with injectable `spawn`. New guards in `autofix-guards.ts` should follow the same `_deps` injection pattern for testability, accepting an optional deps parameter rather than importing `spawn` directly.

userStories.title: Parse mock_structure declarations
acceptanceCriteria: `TestEditDeclaration` union includes `"mock_structure"` as a valid `reason` value, and the interface declares optional `files: string[]` and `reasonDetail: string` fields.

When agent output contains a block beginning `TEST_EDIT_REASON: mock_structure` with `FILES: a.test.ts, b.test.ts` and a non-empty `REASON:`, then `parseTestEditDeclarations(output)` returns a single declaration with `reason === "mock_structure"`, `file === "a.test.ts"`, `files.length === 2`, and `reasonDetail` set to the verbatim REASON paragraph.
When the `mock_structure` block has empty `FILES:` (or the field is missing), then `parseTestEditDeclarations` returns no declaration for that block.
When the `mock_structure` block has missing `REASON:` (or the field is empty), then `parseTestEditDeclarations` returns no declaration for that block.
When `FILES` contains whitespace around commas (`a.test.ts , b.test.ts`), then `files` returns trimmed paths with no surrounding whitespace.
Existing `prd_contract`, `lint_only`, and `sibling_scope` parser behavior is unchanged — every existing test in `test-edit-declaration.test.ts` still passes.
suggestedCriteria: When a `mock_structure` block is followed by another block separated by a blank line, only the content before the blank line is parsed as the block's fields.
When `REASON:` spans multiple lines before the next blank line, all lines after `REASON:` up to the blank line are captured in `reasonDetail`.
When output contains both a `mock_structure` block and a `prd_contract` block separated by blank lines, `parseTestEditDeclarations` returns two independent declarations.

routing.reasoning: Two files, extends existing regex and block-parsing pattern, clear requirements with no new abstractions.

userStories.title: Validate FILES, synthesize virtual findings, stash handoff side-channel
acceptanceCriteria: `PipelineContext` interface declares optional `pendingMockStructureHandoffs?: { files: string[]; reasonDetail: string }[]`.

`validateMockStructureFiles(decls, workdir, resolvedPatterns)` returns `{ valid, invalid }` partition where `valid` contains every `mock_structure` declaration whose every path exists on disk and is classified as a test file by `resolvedPatterns.regex`, and `invalid` contains the others tagged with `missing` and `nonTest` arrays.
`validateMockStructureFiles` passes through non-`mock_structure` declarations unchanged in `valid`.

When `applyTestEditDeclarations` receives a valid `mock_structure` declaration, the returned finding array contains one synthetic finding per path in `decl.files` with `source === "implementer-handoff"`, `severity === "error"`, `category === "test_mock_restructure"`, `fixTarget === "test"`, and `file` set to the path.

When `applyTestEditDeclarations` receives an invalid `mock_structure` declaration (passed in via the `invalid` partition), the returned array contains one advisory finding with `category === "mock_structure_invalid_files"` and `severity === "warning"` whose `message` lists the offending paths.
`applyTestEditDeclarations` returns the original source-tagged findings unchanged in the array — source `fixTarget` is retained on all pre-existing findings.

In the cycle's `validate()` callback, when `ctx.testEditDeclarations` contains `mock_structure` declarations and `validateMockStructureFiles` classifies them as valid, `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs` is populated with `{ files, reasonDetail }` entries (one per valid declaration) before `applyTestEditDeclarations` runs.
After `validate()` completes, `ctx.testEditDeclarations` is cleared (existing behavior preserved).
suggestedCriteria: When `decls` is empty, `validateMockStructureFiles` returns `{ valid: [], invalid: [] }` without making any filesystem calls.
When all declarations are non-`mock_structure`, `validateMockStructureFiles` returns them all in `valid` without making any filesystem calls.
When a `mock_structure` declaration lists three paths but only two exist on disk, `invalid` entry lists the missing path in `missing` and `nonTest` is empty.

routing.reasoning: Multiple modules (pipeline, findings, test-runners), new async validator, new side-channel field, requires careful coordination between pure sync function and async orchestration.

userStories.title: mock-restructure prompt mode and Exception 4
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add Exception 4 to `CONTRADICTION_ESCAPE_HATCH` and a `mock-restructure` rendering mode to `RectifierPromptBuilder.testWriterRectification`.

**Motivation** — The implementer needs prompt guidance for when to use the new escape valve, and the test-writer needs a dedicated prompt template that prohibits assertion changes while allowing mock restructuring.

**Approach** — Two changes, both prompt-only:

1. Extend `CONTRADICTION_ESCAPE_HATCH` in `rectifier-builder-helpers.ts` with Exception 4:
```
### Exception 4 — Mock-structure handoff

Use ONLY when the only path to satisfy the ACs requires a structural test rewrite
that does NOT fit Exception 2. Examples: mocks reference primitives the new code
bypasses; assertion topology must change to match a new dispatch shape.

Declare with:
TEST_EDIT_REASON: mock_structure
FILES: <comma-separated test file paths>
REASON: <one paragraph: which mock is wrong vs which dispatch the new code uses>

Rules:
- Do NOT make any edits yourself; the test-writer will fulfill.
- Do NOT also emit `UNRESOLVED:` in the same turn — this declaration IS the handoff.
- FILES must list real test files. Each path must exist and be a test file.
```

2. Add `_testWriterMockRestructure` private static method as a peer to `_testWriterFixTestFiles` and `_testWriterWriteFailingTest`. Extend `testWriterRectification` to dispatch to it when `mode === "mock-restructure"`. The new rendering:

> "You are restructuring test mocks to align with the AC-mandated dispatch shape.
>
> Story: ${title} (${id})
>
> ### Acceptance Criteria
> ${acList}
>
> ### Files to rewrite (only these)
> ${handoffFiles, one per line}
>
> ### Implementer handoff
> ${handoffReason}
>
> Rules:
> 1. Modify ONLY the files listed above.
> 2. Do NOT modify any source file.
> 3. Do NOT loosen, remove, or rewrite any assertion site (`expect(`, `toBe`, `toEqual`, `toThrow`, `not.`, language equivalents). Restructure mock setup, dispatch wiring, and arrangement only.
> 4. The tests must continue to encode the SPECIFICATION, not the current behavior.
> 5. Commit your changes when done."

**Scope** — In: `src/prompts/builders/rectifier-builder-helpers.ts`, `src/prompts/builders/rectifier-builder.ts`. Out: type changes to `AutofixTestWriterInput` (US-004), strategy wiring (US-004), safety guards (US-005).

**Interface**
```typescript
// Extended signature for testWriterRectification
static testWriterRectification(
  findings: ReviewCheckResult[],
  story: UserStory,
  options?: {
    mode?: "fix-test-files" | "write-failing-test" | "mock-restructure";
    blockingThreshold?: "error" | "warning" | "info";
    /** mock-restructure only */
    handoffReason?: string;
    /** mock-restructure only */
    handoffFiles?: string[];
  },
): string
```
acceptanceCriteria: `CONTRADICTION_ESCAPE_HATCH` text includes a section titled "Exception 4 — Mock-structure handoff" that lists `TEST_EDIT_REASON: mock_structure`, `FILES:`, and `REASON:` as required fields.
`CONTRADICTION_ESCAPE_HATCH` Exception 4 text states the rule: "Do NOT also emit `UNRESOLVED:` in the same turn — this declaration IS the handoff."
`RectifierPromptBuilder.testWriterRectification` accepts `mode: "mock-restructure"` and dispatches to `_testWriterMockRestructure`.

When `testWriterRectification` is called with `mode: "mock-restructure"` and `options.handoffReason` and `options.handoffFiles` set, the returned prompt contains the verbatim `handoffReason` text and lists every entry from `handoffFiles` under a "Files to rewrite (only these)" heading.

The `mock-restructure` prompt explicitly instructs the agent to NOT modify any source file and NOT modify any assertion site — literal substrings "Do NOT modify any source file" and at least one of `expect(`, `toBe`, `toEqual`, `toThrow` are present in the returned prompt.
When `testWriterRectification` is called without a `mode` argument, it returns the existing `_testWriterFixTestFiles` prompt unchanged.
suggestedCriteria: When `testWriterRectification` is called with `mode: "mock-restructure"` but `handoffFiles` is undefined, the prompt renders without throwing.
When `testWriterRectification` is called with `mode: "mock-restructure"` and `handoffFiles` contains three entries, all three appear as separate lines under the files heading.

routing.reasoning: Prompt-only changes in 2 files, purely additive, clear requirements for string content and dispatch logic.

userStories.title: Wire mock-restructure handoff through test-writer strategy
acceptanceCriteria: `AutofixTestWriterInput` interface declares optional `handoffReason: string` and `handoffFiles: string[]` fields and the `mode` union accepts `"mock-restructure"`.

When `buildAutofixStrategies` testWriter `buildInput` is called and `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs` is non-empty, the returned input has `mode === "mock-restructure"`, `handoffFiles` set to the deduplicated union of all `files` arrays across the handoffs, and `handoffReason` set to the `reasonDetail` paragraphs joined with `

---

`.
When `buildInput` consumes `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs`, it clears the side-channel (sets to empty array).
When `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs` is undefined or empty, `buildInput` returns its existing shape (`mode: "fix-test-files"` or `"write-failing-test"` per existing branches).

When `testWriterRectifyOp.build` receives an input with `mode: "mock-restructure"`, it forwards `handoffReason` and `handoffFiles` into the `options` argument of `RectifierPromptBuilder.testWriterRectification`.

Integration test: given a review with one source-targeted finding in `src/foo.ts`, an implementer mock that returns a `mock_structure` declaration with `files: ["test/foo.test.ts"]` on its first call (and `applied: true` on subsequent calls), and a test-writer mock that returns success, then `runAgentRectificationV2` makes at least one implementer call (the first emitting the `mock_structure` declaration) followed by at least one test-writer call where the test-writer's input carries `mode === "mock-restructure"` AND the source finding in `src/foo.ts` was never re-tagged to `fixTarget: "test"` in any callOp input. Note: the implementer may be called again in the same iteration as the test-writer (both strategies are co-run-sequential and apply when both source and synthetic test findings are present); the test must not assert an exact implementer call count.
suggestedCriteria: When `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs` contains two handoffs each listing the same file, `handoffFiles` contains that file exactly once after deduplication.

When `ctx.pendingMockStructureHandoffs` contains two handoffs with different `reasonDetail` values, `handoffReason` contains both paragraphs separated by `

---

`.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module wiring across operations and pipeline stages, integration test spanning the full cycle, new type fields, one-shot consumption semantics.

userStories.title: Safety guards and config flag
acceptanceCriteria: `NaxConfigSchema.parse({})` returns a config where `quality.autofix.enforceTestWriterIsolation === true`.

`assertionSiteDiffCheck(workdir, beforeRef, files)` returns `{ violated: true, file, line, content }` when `git diff --unified=0 <beforeRef> -- <file>` output for any file in `files` contains an added line matching `/expect\(|\.toBe\(|\.toEqual\(|\.toThrow\(|\bnot\.|\.toMatch\(|\bassert\./`.
`assertionSiteDiffCheck` returns `{ violated: false }` when the diff added lines contain no assertion-call patterns (e.g. mock setup, import, comment edits only).

`runIsolationGuard(workdir, beforeRef, config)` calls `verifyTestWriterIsolation` with `config.tdd.testWriterAllowedPaths` and the configured test patterns, and returns `{ violated: true, files: violations }` when the check returns `passed: false`.
`runIsolationGuard` returns `{ violated: false, skipped: true }` when `config.quality.autofix.enforceTestWriterIsolation === false` — the underlying `verifyTestWriterIsolation` is not invoked.

When the autofix test-writer op completes in `mock-restructure` mode and `assertionSiteDiffCheck` returns violated, `runAgentRectificationV2` calls `revertDiff(workdir, handoffFiles)` (which runs `git checkout HEAD -- <files>`) and the iteration's recorded `unresolved` reason starts with `assertion_weakening:`.

When the autofix test-writer op completes in `mock-restructure` mode and `runIsolationGuard` returns violated, `runAgentRectificationV2` calls `revertDiff` against the violated files and the iteration's recorded `unresolved` reason starts with `test_writer_isolation_violation:`.
When both guards pass, the test-writer's commit is retained, the cycle proceeds to validate normally, and no `revertDiff` call occurs.
suggestedCriteria: When `assertionSiteDiffCheck` is called with an empty `files` array, it returns `{ violated: false }` immediately without spawning a git process.
When `revertDiff` is called and `git checkout HEAD -- <files>` exits non-zero, it throws a `NaxError` rather than silently continuing.
When `config.quality.autofix.enforceTestWriterIsolation` is `false` and Guard B would have fired, the cycle logs at `warn` level and retains the commit.

routing.reasoning: New file with safety-critical revert logic, cross-module dependencies (isolation.ts, git.ts, config schema), and post-commit guard coordination with the cycle's exit rails — high risk if guard semantics are wrong.
